newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH INSURERS RISE ON RESTRUCTURING SPECULATION.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH INSURERS RISE ON RESTRUCTURING SPECULATION.

text.p: Shares in Finnish insurance companies were fuelled to sharp gains by speculation that the sector may see some ownership restructuring, brokers said.

At 1230/0930 GMT, Pohjola stood at 91.50 markka, up 2.50 or 2.80 percent, after touching a 94.00 markka two-year-high. Sampo traded at 320.00 markka, up one markka, also off a new two-year-high at 322.00 markka.
The combined volume for the companies was a lively 26 million markka.
Speculation spread on Thursday morning that banking group Merita which has major holdings in both Pohjola and Sampo might be disposing or reducing its stake in the companies.
Brokers said Swedish insurance major Skandia was the most likely buyer.
Demand for Sampo and Pohjola shares was both domestic and foreign.
